narrative:
The model determined that you have a 29% chance of being a bad credit risk. While this is not a high probability, the bank’s decision threshold led to your loan application being denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, your other installment plans, and the length of the loan you requested. Your checking account status was the most important reason for the denial. Because you have no checking account, this pushed the prediction noticeably toward bad credit risk. Among approved applicants, only 59% had no checking account, so this absence stood out as a negative signal.

Your existing installment plan with a bank was the second most influential factor. Having this additional commitment pushed the prediction toward viewing you as higher risk.

The requested loan duration of 12 months worked in your favor. It is well below the 19-month average of approved loans and therefore pulled the prediction toward good credit. Unfortunately, this positive effect was not strong enough to overcome the first two factors.

You should focus on opening and maintaining a checking account for several months before reapplying, and consider whether you can pay off or restructure your existing bank installment plan. These steps would directly address the main reasons your application was declined.
